prompt: Assume constant positive base costs and unit-cost arithmetic. Which explanations of recursive work are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Merge sort does linear total work at each of logarithmically many levels.
options.explanation: Smaller subproblems are offset by more subproblems per level.

options.text: Removing one item per call and doing work proportional to remaining size leads to quadratic total work.
options.explanation: There are linearly many levels, whose work decreases from the full size to one.

options.text: Doubling a smaller task and adding one step always introduces an extra linear multiplier on top of exponential growth.
options.explanation: Hanoi-style doubling gives exponential growth without that extra multiplier.

options.text: Following one half-sized subproblem with constant work per call gives logarithmic work.
options.explanation: Only the number of halvings matters.

options.text: Naive recursive Fibonacci is linear because it has only two base cases.
options.explanation: It repeats overlapping subproblems; memoisation is what removes that repetition.

workedExample: Count levels and total work per level separately. Halving creates logarithmic depth, but a whole level can contain many calls. Removing one item creates linear depth. A branching call tree can repeat smaller tasks exponentially often. Memoisation changes the work by sharing their results, and exact large-integer arithmetic has costs beyond this unit-cost model.
